title: release-provenance --post checks the launcher at X, which a Release run no longer publishes, and the promote-published X launcher carries no provenance
description: Found by the LCLI-616/618 reviewer (2026-09-27), outside that diff; confirmed here by reading scripts/release-provenance.mjs runPost at dev bb8b2662. Since LCLI-621 (ODOC-302), a Release run stages the root launcher as X-rc.N, and the launcher at X reaches npm only later, when scripts/promote-latest.mjs fresh-publishes it --tag latest. release.yml's provenance-post job runs release-provenance.mjs --post, which checks releasePackages() (the launcher plus six platforms) at X. So in a publish:true run it (a) queries @opum-ai/lore@X, which does not exist yet, and (b) never checks the rc launcher the run actually published. It fails only on a dangling commit, so the run does not go red; it just checks the wrong object. Separately and larger: promote-latest publishes the X launcher from the operator's machine with a token, not through OIDC trusted publishing, so the launcher on latest never carries provenance even once LCLI-482 is fixed. The platforms keep whatever provenance their staging publish had. Whether the launcher's final publish should move into CI, to get provenance, is a design question for opum-agent (it touches Article 3.5's promote step and quest-cli's mirror, QCLI-399), not a local fix.

acceptanceCriteria.text: provenance-post (release-provenance.mjs --post) checks the packages a Release run actually published: six platforms at X and the launcher at X-rc.N, never the launcher at X; a test pins the package/version set

The runbook records the X launcher published by promote-latest.mjs as "provenance-missing, byte-bound to the qualified rc" (OPAG-127 AC4 wording), states that the equivalence gate and finalTarball.sha256 bind bytes to the qualified rc and are NOT a substitute for provenance (which attests the workflow, commit and runner), and points at OPAG-127 as the home for restoring provenance on the final publish, for both CLIs
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0; a reviewer pass covers the release.yml / scripts change

plan: 1. release-provenance.mjs: add --launcher-rc N (required for --post, validated ^[1-9][0-9]*$, exit 2 on absent/malformed); --post maps the launcher (manifest.name) to X-rc.N and every other package to X, by name, so the launcher at X is never queried even under a --package override. --pre unchanged.

2. Fix printed text now false: --post header line, job-summary note naming the X launcher as not checked here (provenance-missing, byte-bound to the qualified rc; OPAG-127); in-code comments on --post.
3. release.yml provenance-post: pass inputs.launcher_rc via env into --launcher-rc; update the step comment.

4. Tests: pin the exact --post package/version set (six platforms at X from package.json, launcher at X-rc.N, launcher@X absent from the stub's request log); rc validation fails closed; workflow test pins the rc wiring. Update existing --post tests for rc keys.

5. Runbook Provenance section: X launcher on latest is provenance-missing, byte-bound to the qualified rc; gate+finalTarball.sha256 are not a substitute for provenance; OPAG-127 for both CLIs. CHANGELOG [Unreleased].
6. Gates: bun test, typecheck, lint, bun run lore check, actionlint, lint:shell; win32 preload run of the provenance test; mutation proof (launcher back at X -> set test red).
implementationNotes: RULED (opum-agent, cross-session, 2026-09-27), applying the ruling already on OPAG-127. Read by ref here at opum-agent dev d0557749, .quest/tasks/OPAG-127.json, note stamped 2026-09-27T21:02Z (orchestrator b5630e61). Option (a) for now: the promote-published X launcher carries no provenance. That is OPAG-127's existing gap showing up in a new place, not a new defect and not a blocker. Restoring provenance on the final publish (a CI job with id-token) is in OPAG-127's scope for BOTH CLIs. Do NOT file it as a lore-only task: Article 3.5 needs both CLIs to promote identically. Premise corrected: no current pair package carries provenance at all. OPAG-127 measured the packument key sets (quest 0.10.0/0.11.0, lore 0.11.0, both darwin-arm64 platforms at 0.11.0): no attestations key. So (a) loses nothing the pair has today. Wording ruled: document it as 'provenance-missing, byte-bound to the qualified rc'. Never present the equivalence gate plus the digest as stronger than, or a substitute for, provenance: they answer 'same bytes as tested'; provenance answers 'built where, from what'. AC2 was amended to say so. The provenance-post half stays local, after LCLI-616/618.

LANDED on branch fix/LCLI-625-provenance-post-rc-launcher at 38e3980d (not yet a PR; reviewer pass pending, AC3). AC1: release-provenance.mjs --post now requires --launcher-rc N (^[1-9][0-9]*$, exit 2 when missing or malformed, and refused on --pre) and assigns versions by package NAME via postReleaseSpecs: the launcher (package.json name) at X-rc.N, every optionalDependencies platform at X. release.yml provenance-post passes LAUNCHER_RC=${{ inputs.launcher_rc }} as --launcher-rc "$LAUNCHER_RC". Each --post run prints (log and job summary) that @opum-ai/lore@X is NOT checked and is provenance-missing, byte-bound to the qualified rc (OPAG-127). Evidence: test/release-provenance.test.ts 'the default set is the six platforms at X and the launcher at X-rc.N, and nothing else' pins the stub's attestation request log to exactly 6 platforms@0.8.0 plus @opum-ai/lore@0.8.0-rc.2, asserts @opum-ai/lore@0.8.0 was never requested, and the stub attests the launcher at X with a destroyed commit so a regression also exits 1. MUTATION: setting the launcher's version back to X in postReleaseSpecs alone -> bun test test/release-provenance.test.ts 13 fail / 27 pass (exit 1), including all three set tests; restored -> 40 pass (exit 0). AC2: runbook 'Provenance and attestations' gains 'The X launcher on latest is provenance-missing, byte-bound to the qualified rc': equivalence gate + finalTarball.sha256 answer 'same bytes as tested', provenance answers 'built where, from what' (workflow, commit, runner), not a substitute and not stronger; OPAG-127 owns restoring it for both CLIs.
